newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA KWV DISAPPOINTED BY PRIVATISATION DELAY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA KWV DISAPPOINTED BY PRIVATISATION DELAY.

text.p: South African wine co-operative KWV on Thursday reacted with "great disappointment" to Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom's court bid to delay its conversion into a company and warned against possible attempts to nationalise its assets.
But it said in a statement that it still hoped to be able to meet the original April 30 deadline for transforming the co-operative into a private company.

"After the overwhelming support by KWV's wine farmer members for its plans to convert to a company, the organisation learnt with great disappointment that the Minister of Agriculture had applied to the Supreme Court for a delay in the ratification of his decision," KWV said.
After intense negotiations in the Supreme Court, the two parties agreed that both applications be postponed until March 25 so that they could make further representations.
One of the concerns expressed by Hanekom had been the question of how privatisation would affect the statutory nature of the co-operative, which regulates the wine industry.
"KWV has, however, already indicated that these statutory powers could be exercised in partnership with the producing wholesale trade and the state," the statement said.
This would mean that the partnership would have to "stand in for the responsibilities and costs of surplus (wine) removal".
Hanekom also expressed concern that KWV's assets, gathered under state protection and special benefits such as tax holidays, would be distributed to the co-operative's members.
"In this regard, it is KWV's considered opinion that these assets are the inalienable property of its 4,751 wine farmer members," KWV said.
"Any actions by the state to the contrary could be construed as an act of nationalisation."
It said it would keep its members briefed on developments and noted that Hanekom had also said that he hoped that the matter would be resolved through negotiation.
